inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,831 Python str.splitlines() logical lines of the normalized 27-page article after confirming the frozen SHA-256 and 131,788-byte size. The source is mathematically rich: it separates finite-height, intermediate, and asymptotic zero-free regimes; exposes the smoothed zero-detector and error-budget mechanism; records two distinct extremal contradiction arguments; and documents how non-negative trigonometric polynomials and auxiliary smoothing functions control explicit constants. Prose is coherent throughout, while several displayed formulas contain text-layer control-character splits and the coefficient tables retain page-layout dependencies, so exact constants in those spans require scan comparison before downstream formula-level use.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the three explicit zero-free improvements and their height ranges; surrounding metadata is non-mathematical.

sections_inspected.label: 1 Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the classical and Korobov–Vinogradov regimes, compares prior constants, states Theorems 1.1–1.4, identifies improvement levers, and splices the best known regions by height.

sections_inspected.label: 2 Some immediate applications
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transfers improved zero-free constants to primes between cubes and the prime-number-theorem error exponent.

sections_inspected.label: 3 Preliminaries
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Collects near-one-line, critical-line, trigonometric-polynomial, and zero-counting inputs used by the detector arguments.

sections_inspected.label: 4 Required lemmas
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the zero-detector, autoconvolution smoothing kernel, Laplace-transform remainder bounds, zero-count estimates, and the combined inequality for a hypothetical zero.

sections_inspected.label: 5 Proof of Theorem 1.1
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Splices finite regimes, assumes an extremal high zero, derives a zero-free rectangle, normalizes error terms, and closes a computer-assisted monotonicity contradiction.

sections_inspected.label: 6 Proof of Theorem 1.4
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reconfigures the detector on fixed half-lines, proves the intermediate-region inequality, and closes a second extremal contradiction.

sections_inspected.label: 7 Proof of Theorem 1.2
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Passes to the asymptotic limit and extracts the improved constant from the degree-46 polynomial.

sections_inspected.label: 8 Computations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Turns polynomial admissibility into an optimization objective, guarantees non-negativity by autocorrelation factorization, and reports the annealing search and certificates.

sections_inspected.label: 9 The classical zero-free region
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Compares smoothing families and combines a higher RH verification, a degree-16 polynomial, and an improved auxiliary function in an iterative constant refinement.

sections_inspected.label: 10 Future work
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Proposes a conditional inductive envelope of finite zero-free regions and identifies the presently unavailable local exclusion tool.

sections_inspected.label: Back matter and references
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Acknowledgements, provenance metadata, bibliography, and publisher note; no new mathematical argument.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Analytic inputs compiled into a zero-exclusion inequality
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Near-one growth, zero counting, a two-line detector, and an autoconvolution smoother are modular inputs that compile into one inequality constraining any zero close to the 1-line.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The compilation is constant-sensitive and several displayed formulas need scan verification; it does not itself establish a zero-free region without a scale choice and extremal argument.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Critical-line information becomes a finite-range bridge
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A sub-Weyl bound can be inserted into a fixed-half-line detector, whose cancellation and transform monotonicity yield an intermediate region strong enough to bridge finite and asymptotic regimes.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The resulting O(1/log t) geometry is deliberately not asymptotically optimal and depends on the stated explicit critical-line estimate.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Constraint-preserving search for proof auxiliaries
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Autocorrelation factorization turns global polynomial non-negativity into a built-in invariant, allowing heuristic search to optimize proof constants while retaining an explicit coefficient certificate.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Simulated annealing and diminishing returns do not certify a global optimum, and rounded table values require rendered-page verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Finite local exclusion as a bootstrap to global zero-free regions
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: An extremal hypothetical zero supplies its own zero-free rectangle; a certified finite boundary region can therefore seed a self-improving contradiction and, conditionally, a sequence of regions whose envelope extends globally.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The proposed many-region generalization remains conditional because current methods cannot exclude zeros in all required high finite rectangles.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Orthogonal gains in the classical-region iteration
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Verified RH height, trigonometric-polynomial choice, secondary-term tuning, and smoothing-family choice enter as separable improvement channels that can be combined and partially ablated.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source imports the full iterative method from prior work and reports computational outputs; this unit family is not a self-contained re-verification.
